_meta.whatThisIs: A catalogue of the Windows API declarations and legacy Type records found across the workspaces, so a refactor can replace a hand-rolled declaration with the one DataFlex already ships, and a legacy Type with a verified Struct.
RULES: COMMENT OUT a replaced declaration, never delete it - the diff stays reversible and the original argument list stays readable next to its replacement.
legacyFields is PROVENANCE, not a layout. It is what the old 32-bit-era Type said, recorded so a human can compare - it is not what should be emitted.
NOTHING may be emitted from an entry whose verified flag is false. A wrong struct is memory corruption at runtime with no compile error, which is the one failure this catalogue could cause.

x86 and x64 layouts are separate and both are needed: the pointer-bearing structures differ in size AND in padding. DataFlex's own Dftypes.pkg shows the idiom - an iMissingAlignment Field inside #IFDEF IS$WIN64.
An ...A entry point is the ANSI form. Prefer the W form DataFlex ships; it is the Unicode-correct one.
_meta.NOT_A_STRUCT_CATALOGUE: The struct layouts live in AppSrc/Win32StructCatalog.inc (34 shapes, the SDK C prototype verbatim) and are read through Win32StructBody - that is the one canonical home and this file does not repeat it. I duplicated it here on 2026-08-26 by building a layout table without checking whether one existed; it did, since 08-09, and the .inc design is better because it keeps the C source of truth and derives DataFlex types at conversion time.
_meta.whatThisAdds: The CORPUS, which the catalogues do not have: what the workspaces on C: actually declare. Which Windows APIs appear and how often, which of them DataFlex 26 already ships and in which package (the complement of Win32ApiCatalog.inc, which by design lists only what DataFlex does NOT declare), and the legacy Type names found in the wild - the evidence that house prefixes like vtBrowseInfo were hiding catalogued shapes from the lookup.
